audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator and balance-sheet bridge straddle completed 2026 acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: $869.6 million aggregate consideration for Thermolec, Crawford and Neptronic; $340.0 million Neptronic borrowing; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 OE anchor excludes all three acquisitions, the June 2026 bridge includes Thermolec and Crawford financing and cash effects, and the bridge predates Neptronic's cash use, debt and earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition was funded through cash on hand and borrowings on our revolving credit facilities under our Amended Credit Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. The acquisitions total $869.6 million against base equity value of $4,726.0 million, so they are large enough to alter the valuation materially. Direction is mixed because omitted acquired earnings understate value, while stale cash and omitted post-acquisition interest, integration costs and other claims overstate it. The record does not quantify Neptronic earnings or a complete common-equity OE adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE and the bridge on a single post-Neptronic date using pro-forma operating cash generation, interest, integration costs, working capital, cash, debt and the completed Crawford non-core sale; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Filtran and COLI returns may be capitalized in earnings and counted again in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.2 million pretax income; approximately $22.1 million after tax and $6.07 per base-case share if fully perpetuated; $117.6 million bridge assets
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained $23.0 million Filtran gain and $5.2 million COLI income inflate OE while the $58.2 million Filtran interest and $59.4 million COLI asset are separately included in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income (expense), net, for 2025 was composed primarily of gains of $23.0 related to changes in the net asset value of our equity interest in Filtran, income of $5.2 derived from COLI policies and a gain of $0.4 related to the settlement of our interest rate swaps which were settled commensurate with the amendment of our Amended Credit Agreement, partially offset by (i) environmental remediation charges of $9.1, (ii) pension and postretirement expense of $8.2 (including net settlement and actuarial losses of $5.8), and (iii) foreign currency transaction losses of $2.5.
audit_findings.explanation: The $117.6 million bridge amount equals the filed Filtran and COLI values, but retention of their income in the anchor is not demonstrated without the adjustment ledger. Even assuming the full $28.2 million was retained and perpetuated, the computed base-case effect is about $6.07 per share, versus the $103.76 gap between base value of $92.61 and market price of $196.37; it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE adjustment ledger and remove the Filtran gain, COLI income and $0.4 million swap gain if present; document the resulting rerun even though the conclusion should remain unchanged.

audit_findings.title: KTS retention compensation could be wrongly stripped as acquisition amortization
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.2 million pretax; approximately $18.9 million after tax and $5.21 per base-case share if fully added back and perpetuated
audit_findings.mechanism: An improper add-back would raise the OE anchor even though the charge compensates employees for future service and is an economic operating cost.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we recognized compensation costs of $ 24.2 which have been recorded to “Selling, general and administrative” within our consolidated statements of operations, related to such retention agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that $24.2 million was employee compensation recorded in SG&A and separately identifies it among acquisition-related costs. The valuation ledger does not demonstrate that it was stripped. At the maximum stated exposure, the computed base-case effect is about $5.21 per share, far below the $103.76 base-value-to-price gap, so it does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the ledger retains the entire $24.2 million charge and future service-period expense; if it was added back, reverse the add-back and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded benefit obligation may represent an unbridged senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $92.8 million net liability, equal to $1.82 per diluted share and 2.0% of base equity value; OE normalization difference unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any pension cash requirement not represented by recurring expense reduces OE; alternatively, an unfunded residual claim may require a bridge deduction before attributing value to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our net liability to these plans was $92.8.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $92.8 million net benefit liability but not that accounting expense understates normalized cash cost. Even deducting the entire liability from the bridge would reduce base value by only $1.82 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged. A separate OE cash-versus-expense mismatch remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile recurring pension and postretirement expense with the filed $14.2 million of 2025 contributions and direct payments and the projected funding schedule; normalize OE for any persistent difference and avoid duplicating it in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may rely on capital spending excluded from normalized owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $135.0-$165.0 million expected 2026 capex; $92.1 million 2025 capex including $62.0 million expansion; computed first-year reinvestment of $0.0 million, $13.8 million and $27.7 million at 0%, 3% and 6% growth using 68.5% RONTA
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth requires incremental capital; excluding expansion capex from normalized OE while deducting insufficient reinvestment through RONTA would overstate forecast distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect 2026 capital expenditures to approximate $135.0 to $165.0, with a significant portion related to upgrades to existing, and continued expansion into the new manufacturing facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The expansion program and spending amounts are demonstrated, but gross capex cannot be equated directly with annual economic reinvestment because it includes maintenance and may fund capacity for several years. The supplied record does not show whether the RONTA deductions adequately fund the scenario growth, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Provide the maintenance-versus-expansion capex schedule, capacity commissioned, expected incremental after-tax operating earnings and useful period; compare those economics with each scenario's RONTA reinvestment deductions and rerun if the deductions are insufficient.

audit_findings.title: The purported share ceiling does not include maximum PSU settlement
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.355 million combined PSU/RSU inventory; an additional 0.355 million shares in the extreme assumption that all are PSUs settling at 200% would reduce base value from $92.61 to approximately $91.98 per share; March 2026 grants unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Understating maximum PSU settlement and omitting later grants understates the diluted-share denominator and therefore overstates per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in long-term incentive compensation expense in 2025, compared to 2024, was due primarily to (i) an increase in the fair value of performance-based share awards resulting from plan design changes effected beginning in 2024, which increased the maximum potential payout range from 150% to 200% of target, (ii) the accumulation of awards related to recent changes in certain key management positions, and (iii) the immediate vesting of awards as a result of executive officers reaching retirement eligibility, partially offset by the impact of forfeitures from participant departures.
audit_findings.explanation: The denominator is not a demonstrated ceiling because the PSU/RSU split and March 2026 grant quantities are absent. However, grossing the entire filed 0.355 million inventory to 200%—a deliberately conservative bound—reduces base value by only about $0.63 per share and cannot change the conclusion relative to the $196.37 market price. The undisclosed 2026 grants remain unquantified but would have to be implausibly large relative to the filed award inventory to bridge the valuation gap.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the PSU/RSU split and March 2, 2026 grant counts, apply award-specific maximum payouts and update the denominator; relabel 51.027 million as an estimate rather than a ceiling until completed.
